Full test suite passes (1418 tests, OK).

I found that every other nested routine resource (`SlotViewSet`, `RoutineDayViewSet`, config viewsets, etc.) validates ownership of *all* foreign keys a client can supply via `get_owner_objects()`, but `WorkoutSessionViewSet` only validated the `routine` FK and never checked `day`. Since `WorkoutSession.day` is a writable, nullable FK to another user's `Day` object, an authenticated user could create/update a workout session referencing a `Day` belonging to someone else's private routine — an authorization bypass through a user-controlled key (IDOR), inconsistent with the ownership-check pattern used everywhere else in this API. I added `(Day, 'day')` to `get_owner_objects()` in `wger/manager/api/views.py`, so the existing `WgerOwnerObjectModelViewSet.create`/`update` ownership check now also rejects cross-user `day` references, matching the hardened pattern used by all sibling viewsets.
